rows.see: how to know the agentic loop is done / when to terminate
rows.answer: check the deterministic `stop_reason` field — never text presence, iteration caps, or “task complete” phrasing

rows.see: prevent the agent returning text (force a tool)
rows.answer: don't force `tool_choice:'any'` to stop text — it causes infinite loops; stop on `stop_reason`

rows.see: coverage gaps in a multi-agent system / subagents missed things
rows.answer: fix the coordinator's decomposition — don't blame subagents or add more

rows.see: make subagents talk to each other / share memory
rows.answer: no — subagents are isolated; they communicate only through the coordinator and don't inherit its history

rows.see: subagent can't see the coordinator's history / other outputs
rows.answer: pass complete context explicitly (incl. metadata) — nothing is auto-shared

rows.see: missing citations in the synthesis output
rows.answer: root cause is context passed without metadata, not the synthesis agent

rows.see: independent tasks running one after another
rows.answer: parallelise — issue parallel Task calls in one response

rows.see: `fork_session` vs `--resume`
rows.answer: `--resume` = continue; `fork_session` = explore divergent branches

rows.see: high-stakes compliance must not fail / drop to 0%
rows.answer: deterministic enforcement (a hook) — not a stronger prompt / few-shot / routing (those stay probabilistic)

rows.see: block a policy-violating action before it runs
rows.answer: a PreToolUse hook (blocks before). PostToolUse is too late — the action already ran

rows.see: normalise / transform tool output consistently
rows.answer: a PostToolUse hook (after) — not model-side transformation

rows.see: handing off to a human
rows.answer: carry every critical field (customer ID, recommended action) — the human can't see the transcript

rows.see: attention dilution / the model loses focus across many files
rows.answer: multi-pass decomposition (+ a cross-batch integration pass) — not a bigger model or larger window

rows.see: open-ended investigation
rows.answer: an adaptable flow, not a fixed pipeline

rows.see: only 3 of 50 files changed
rows.answer: fresh start + inject a summary of the 3 — don't re-explore everything or `--resume` (stale tool results)

rows.see: the agent picks the wrong tool / misroutes
rows.answer: clarify and enrich the tool descriptions first — they're the primary selection mechanism (not few-shot or a classifier)

rows.see: a tool failed — how should the agent recover
rows.answer: return structured error metadata (`errorCategory`, `isRetryable`, `description`) so the agent picks the right recovery

rows.see: empty result from a *successful* query
rows.answer: don't retry — a valid empty result isn't a failure

rows.see: the agent has too many tools (e.g. 18) / unreliable selection
rows.answer: ~4–5 role-specific tools per agent (scope cross-role tools)

rows.see: structured output is required
rows.answer: a `tool_choice` that guarantees a call — `'auto'` may return text

rows.see: MCP available to the whole team
rows.answer: project `.mcp.json` (committed). `~/.claude.json` is user-level / personal

rows.see: a standard integration (e.g. Jira)
rows.answer: use the existing/standard MCP server — don't build a custom one

rows.see: secrets in the MCP config
rows.answer: env-var expansion `${VAR}` — never commit credentials

rows.see: find where a function is called / search file *contents*
rows.answer: Grep (searches contents). Glob searches paths

rows.see: find files by name / extension pattern
rows.answer: Glob (paths). Grep is for contents

rows.see: modify a file
rows.answer: try Edit first; widen context on a non-unique match before escalating to Read + Write

rows.see: do all tool definitions load at connection time?
rows.answer: no (with tool search on, the default) — only names + server instructions load; full schemas are deferred / on-demand

rows.see: expose read-only data
rows.answer: a resource (app-controlled), not a tool — a tool causes exploratory calls

rows.see: many objects share the same shape
rows.answer: one templated resource URI (`db://tables/{name}/schema`), not one resource per object

rows.see: shared with team / all developers / no manual setup
rows.answer: project-level `.claude/…`, committed to git

rows.see: a new hire gets no instructions, same repo
rows.answer: instructions live in personal `~/.claude/` (not in git) — move them to project-level

rows.see: first diagnostic step — works for one dev, not another
rows.answer: the `/memory` command — shows which files are actually loaded

rows.see: guarantee / always / at every save / regardless of what Claude does
rows.answer: a hook (auto-script on an event). Never CLAUDE.md / a rule / “mark as important”

rows.see: two rules conflict, must always hold
rows.answer: a hook / `settings.json` (CLAUDE.md has no hard precedence)

rows.see: CLAUDE.md has grown to 400–500 lines, all mixed together
rows.answer: split it: `@import` external files, or a `.claude/rules/` folder by topic

rows.see: available to the whole team (command / skill)
rows.answer: `.claude/commands/` or `.claude/skills/` + git

rows.see: personal, without affecting teammates
rows.answer: `~/.claude/…` (personal folder)

rows.see: noisy output / exploration clutters the conversation / keep the full analysis
rows.answer: `context: fork` (the skill runs in a separate context; only the summary returns)

rows.see: a rule must ALWAYS apply automatically
rows.answer: NOT a skill (a skill runs only when invoked) — use a hook

rows.see: conventions for one file type scattered across 50+ folders (.tf, SQL, Java)
rows.answer: `.claude/rules/` with a glob (`paths: ["**/*.test.tsx"]`)

rows.see: …rather than a CLAUDE.md in every folder
rows.answer: correct — a glob is better: one place, auto-loads, saves context

rows.see: multi-file / architecture / migration of 30–60 files
rows.answer: plan mode (plan first)

rows.see: single-file fix, clear stack trace, one `if`
rows.answer: direct execution (just do it)

rows.see: new to the domain / requirements unclear
rows.answer: interview — Claude asks clarifying questions first

rows.see: design first, then implement
rows.answer: plan → direct

rows.see: isolate noisy code exploration
rows.answer: a subagent (context isolation)

rows.see: Claude reads the description differently each time
rows.answer: give 2 concrete examples → done (don't rewrite the prose) — few-shot

rows.see: complex transform with many edge cases
rows.answer: give Claude failing tests first (this is iterative refinement / TDD)

rows.see: edits are independent of each other
rows.answer: give them one at a time

rows.see: edits affect each other
rows.answer: give them all in one message

rows.see: the `claude` script hangs / waits for input
rows.answer: the `-p` flag (non-interactive mode)

rows.see: need a machine-readable result for auto-comments
rows.answer: `--output-format json`

rows.see: reviewing its own code in the same session
rows.answer: not allowed — a separate, independent Claude run for review

rows.see: re-review after new commits, don't duplicate comments
rows.answer: feed prior findings into context + “report only what's new”

rows.see: add one or two rules, keep normal Claude
rows.answer: `--append-system-prompt` (adds on top)

rows.see: the root persona is wrong (e.g. a release-notes generator starts running tests)
rows.answer: `--system-prompt` (replaces entirely)

rows.see: same, but text from a file
rows.answer: the `…-file` variants

rows.see: skip ALL auto-load (CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks, MCP) — fast repeated calls
rows.answer: `--bare`

rows.see: use ONLY the MCP from this config, drop the rest
rows.answer: `--strict-mcp-config`

rows.see: too many false positives in review
rows.answer: explicit categorical criteria (exactly what to flag/skip) + code examples — not “be conservative” or confidence thresholds

rows.see: inconsistent output formatting / detailed instructions didn't work
rows.answer: few-shot examples (with reasoning) — the most effective first intervention, not “more instructions”

rows.see: guarantee a tool call / structured output
rows.answer: `tool_choice:'any'` guarantees a call; `'auto'` may return text

rows.see: does a JSON schema prevent all extraction errors?
rows.answer: no — it kills syntax errors only; semantic correctness still needs validation

rows.see: the model fabricates values when the source lacks info
rows.answer: make fields optional / nullable — not all-required

rows.see: extraction failed — retry
rows.answer: resend {original doc + failed extraction + the specific error}; blind retries repeat the mistake

rows.see: the information is genuinely absent
rows.answer: can't be retried into existence — retries fix format/structure, not missing data

rows.see: cut cost — move everything to batch
rows.answer: batch only for latency-tolerant async work; keep blocking/real-time & multi-turn flows synchronous (batch: 50% cost, up to 24h)

rows.see: review its own code in the same session
rows.answer: an independent instance (no prior context) — self-review's retained reasoning won't question itself

rows.see: large multi-file review
rows.answer: per-file passes + a separate cross-file integration pass — not a single pass or a bigger-context model

rows.see: long conversation with transactional data (numbers / dates / IDs)
rows.answer: extract facts into a persistent structured facts block sent every prompt — summarisation destroys them

rows.see: “lost in the middle”
rows.answer: a structural fix — key facts first + section headers, not “pay attention”

rows.see: the customer is frustrated / angry
rows.answer: sentiment isn't a signal — escalate on explicit signals only (human request, policy gap, can't advance)

rows.see: self-reported confidence as an escalation signal
rows.answer: poorly calibrated — not a valid escalation signal

rows.see: an explicit human request to escalate
rows.answer: escalate immediately — don't try to resolve first

rows.see: an ambiguous customer match
rows.answer: ask for more identifiers — don't guess via heuristics (privacy risk)

rows.see: a subagent times out / errors
rows.answer: propagate structured error context (type, action, partial results, alternatives); don't return empty-as-success or kill the whole pipeline

rows.see: context degradation exploring a large codebase
rows.answer: an attention-quality problem — scratchpad files, subagent context isolation, state manifests; not a bigger window

rows.see: why delegate to a subagent
rows.answer: the primary benefit is context isolation, not just parallelisation

rows.see: 97% aggregate accuracy — automate everything?
rows.answer: validate per document-type / field (one type could be 40%); calibrate on labelled data

rows.see: which items to send for human review
rows.answer: stratified sampling on the highest-uncertainty items — not only low-confidence, not spread evenly

rows.see: two credible sources conflict
rows.answer: annotate both with source + date and let the consumer decide — don't pick the most recent

rows.see: different numbers across sources
rows.answer: not necessarily contradictions — different dates explain them; require dates in the output

rows.see: the synthesis agent paraphrases
rows.answer: preserve claim→source mappings through the pipeline — attribution dies in summarisation
